# Tauri shell, Rust core, React webview, bun for development

> Everything reusable from prior work is presentation and everything new is systems work, so the split falls exactly where the toolchain boundary already is.

Applies to `app/**`, `crates/**`, `web/**`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **Electron** (nothing refuses it) — The weight lands exactly where this machine is already tight, and it would still end in a separate Node daemon.
- **Wails, with Go** (nothing refuses it) — Go is a better fit for the concurrent half and cross-compiles beautifully, but v3 is in alpha and v2 is the previous generation.
- **Rust everywhere, WASM frontend** (nothing refuses it) — Elegant, and it kills the plugin story: nobody writes a Rust plugin for a personal tool.
- **Elixir and LiveView** (nothing refuses it) — OTP supervises BEAM processes beautifully and OS processes awkwardly, and this product's core job is the second. LiveView also conflicts with a client-side plugin contract.
- **Svelte instead of React** (nothing refuses it) — Better shape fit for a live-updating queue, but the advantage is theoretical at 5–20 items, and mature editor tooling matters twice here.
- **Business logic in the webview** (refused by `seam/commands-live-together`) — The seam has to stay one folder of commands somebody can read in a sitting, or the Rust core stops being the core.

## What keeps it

- `seam/every-invoke-names-a-command`
- `seam/commands-live-together`
